mark_breakdown.desc: Apply change of base rule to base 9

subparts.solution: $\log_{\frac{1}{9}} x = \log_9 5 \implies \frac{\log_9 x}{\log_9\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)} = \log_9 5 \implies \frac{\log_9 x}{\log_9(9^{-1})} = \log_9 5 \implies \frac{\log_9 x}{-1} = \log_9 5 \implies \log_9 x = -\log_9 5 \implies \log_9 x = \log_9(5^{-1}) \implies x = 5^{-1} = \frac{1}{5}$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Change of base formula: $\log_b x = \frac{\log_c x}{\log_c b}$.
step_by_step: Change base of $\log_{1/9} x$ to base 9: $\frac{\log_9 x}{\log_9(1/9)}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Incorrectly equating $x = 5$ by ignoring the base difference.

mark_breakdown.desc: Use change of base to convert $\log_8 x$ to base 2
Express $x$ in exact simplified radical form

subparts.solution: $\log_2 x - \log_8 x = 3 \implies \log_2 x - \frac{\log_2 x}{\log_2 8} = 3 \implies \log_2 x - \frac{\log_2 x}{3} = 3 \implies \frac{2}{3}\log_2 x = 3 \implies \log_2 x = \frac{9}{2} \implies x = 2^{\frac{9}{2}} = 2^4 \times 2^{\frac{1}{2}} = 16\sqrt{2}$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Convert different bases to a common base using change of base: $\log_8 x = \frac{\log_2 x}{3}$.
step_by_step: Convert $\log_8 x$ to base 2: $\frac{\log_2 x}{\log_2 8} = \frac{1}{3}\log_2 x$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Evaluating $2^{9/2}$ as $2^4 + 2^{1/2}$ or leaving as unsimplified decimal.

mark_breakdown.desc: Collect and simplify coefficients of $\log_3 x$

subparts.solution: $\log_{27}(x^4) = \log_9 x - \log_3(\sqrt[5]{9}) \implies \frac{\log_3(x^4)}{\log_3 27} = \frac{\log_3 x}{\log_3 9} - \log_3(3^{\frac{2}{5}}) \implies \frac{\log_3(x^4)}{\log_3(3^3)} = \frac{\log_3 x}{\log_3(3^2)} - \log_3(3^{\frac{2}{5}}) \implies \frac{4\log_3 x}{3} = \frac{\log_3 x}{2} - \frac{2}{5} \implies \log_3 x\left(\frac{4}{3} - \frac{1}{2}\right) = -\frac{2}{5} \implies \frac{5}{6}\log_3 x = -\frac{2}{5} \implies \log_3 x = -\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{6}{5} = -\frac{12}{25} \implies x = 3^{-\frac{12}{25}} = \frac{1}{3^{\frac{12}{25}}}$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Express all terms with a common base of 3 using the change of base theorem.
